Well I can make a rough estimate.

Assuming that the guy placed the rear wheels on the jackstands and was working on the engine, that the car conforms to these dimensions, and an idealized case where we assume the center of gravity is roughly 10 inches behind the driver seat (engine/transmission location) and that the entire weight of the car acts through that point, and that the car behaves as if simply supported:

Then by summation of moments about the front wheels on the ground (and assuming both back wheels are on jackstands), then the force on each jackstand will be approximately 929 lb for the 2072 lb car weight total, not 500 lb. The remainder of the weight (214 lb) is supported by the front tires.

The exact center of gravity of the car however will likely be more forward of the engine, somewhere in the passenger compartment, in which case the actual force on the jackstands will be lower, probably more around 750 to 800 lb each.
